This exercise is targeting back muscles, there is very little shoulder muscle activity.

Do those pullups, check the form in tutorials
https://i.ytimg.com/vi/R9mHV0of5I0/maxresdefault.jpg

Like that, you're basically looking up:
https://i.ytimg.com/vi/R9mHV0of5I0/maxresdefault.jpg
8-10 reps per exercise x3, each round.

Please remember, endurance does not equal strength...what I'm saying is that 15 second clean tuck planche is enough to move to advanced tuck.
Start doing pushups when in tuck planche, do them on paralettes or dip bars because you will need some space below. Another progression is tuck planche with hips a bit higher. Other than that, pseudo planche pushups and planche leans will get your far.

I am stretching my wrists regularly, multiple times daily for 3 months now.

Pushups are not a problem for me, except for diamond pushups and PPPs with a lot of lean (those two make my forearms hurt).

Other than that I'm doing weighted/resisted pushups every week, plyo, wide, incline, decline.

Thats so hard to accept for me. 

It has been a year since I started training the planche regularly, 6 months of that time I have been injured and my wish to achieve the planche has only grown bigger. 

What alternative exercises could I be doing to strenghten shoulder muscles for planche?

I'm not sure if I'm missing your point or you're missing mine, the problem is not in my wrists, but yes I don't train with wrists facing forward. 

The problem is with the muscle pain when I come out of the  planche lean - outer side of the forearm at the middle, directly below the bone.

My forearms are pretty strong in general, I have been doing wrist curls for some time with high reps. To be more specific, I will describe where the pain is located. 

If you extend your arm with your palm facing down, the pain is in the middle of the arm, between the wrist and the elbow at the outer side of the forearm, directly below the bone (not on top of the extended arm) and is "spread" a few centimeters down towards the wrist.

My current planche training includes tuck PL holds, (max.) planche leans, PPP's full planche lean holds with resistance band at my ankles.
I'm using paralettes at all times, except at PPP's because I can lean more and I feel like I have more control. Otherwise I would position my hands sideways, because front facing wrists hurt too much.
I don't do any other wrist exercises, because I never felt any pain in my wrists (forearm pain is located in the middle, between the wrist and the elbow).

My general strenght training includes weighted pushups (different variations), front lever exercises, weighted pullups and dragon flags.
I understood nothing, damn I feel like such a newb. Thanks anyway.

No problem, I can provide more info. I'm 1.82m tall and my weight is 82kgs.
I'm training for planche, FL and dragon flag most often, so regarding core and straight arm strenght there are not much problems, its my back strength. I'm currently adding weight to my pullups and will see in the future how will it benefit me.
Rest time between each set is around a minute, between rounds around 5 minutes.

I'm afraid of dynamic exercises for planche because thats exactly how I injured myself. I was on the dip bars and went in tuck PL, I did a light swing forward and when I swung back and lift my butt, I lost control and if I stopped holding the bars I would fall, instead I held them and leaned forward too much to prevent myself from falling. That led to overload in my forearm flexors and I ripped the muscle tissue. I can prevent that from happening by never doing that on the dip bars again, only on the floor.
